questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The inspectors were examining the safety protocols when the alarm was triggered.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The inspectors were examining the safety protocols when the alarm was triggered.
options_en: The safety protocols were examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols were being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols had been examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols are being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
options_hi: The safety protocols were examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols were being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols had been examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols are being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Past Continuous Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Past Continuous tense, the active structure is:
Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + was/were + being + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “being” is compulsory in continuous passive constructions. The auxiliary (was/were) must agree with the new subject, and the main verb must be converted into its past participle (V³) form.

Here, “were examining” is in Past Continuous tense.
“The safety protocols” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is plural, we use “were”. In continuous passive constructions, “being” must be added after the auxiliary. The verb “examining” changes to its past participle form “examined”.

Hence, “were being examined” is the correct transformation.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Being” is mandatory in continuous passive forms.
Use “was” for singular subjects and “were” for plural subjects.
Always convert V-ing to V³ in passive voice.
Do not convert continuous tense into simple past while converting.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: She is widely regarded as one of the few elite
marathon athletes who has consistently qualified
for the final round of the international championships.
No Error
options_hi: She is widely regarded as one of the few elite
marathon athletes who has consistently qualified
for the final round of the international championships.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “has” with “have”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Relative Pronouns with "One of the..."

When the structure "one of the + plural noun + relative pronoun (who/which/that)" is used, the relative pronoun refers to the plural noun (the antecedent) that immediately precedes it. Because the relative pronoun represents a plural group, the verb that follows must also be in the plural form

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the relative pronoun "who" refers to the plural antecedent "athletes." Even though the sentence begins by focusing on "She," the clause introduced by "who" is describing the entire group of elite athletes she belongs to. Therefore, the singular verb "has" is grammatically incorrect and must be replaced with the plural verb "have."

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 : He is one of those leaders who inspire everyone around them.

Example 2 : This is one of the innovations that have changed the world forever.

Example 3 : It was one of the scams which were exposed by the media last month.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

-The "Only" Trap: If the sentence had said "She is the only one of the athletes...", then the verb would be singular (has). Without "the only," the verb is always plural.

-Identify the Antecedent: Always ignore the "One of" and look at the noun right before "who/which/that." That noun dictates the verb's number.

-Mental Check: Ask yourself: Who has qualified? In this context, it is the group of "athletes" (of which she is one). Since "athletes" is plural, "have" is mandatory.

The artisan explained that while the intricate decorative carvings were ___________ solid mahogany, the specialized varnish used to protect them was ___________ a secret blend of resin and alcohol.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The artisan explained that while the intricate decorative carvings were ___________ solid mahogany, the specialized varnish used to protect them was ___________ a secret blend of resin and alcohol.
options_en: made from / made of
made of / made from
made of / made of
made from / made from
options_hi: made from / made of
made of / made from
made of / made of
made from / made from
questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: (Made of vs. Made from)

In competitive exams, the distinction between these two depends on whether the transformation of the material is physical or chemical:

Application to the Given Question

"...carvings were made of solid mahogany, the specialized varnish... was made from a secret blend of resin and alcohol."

In the first part, the carvings are still mahogany; the wood hasn't changed its chemical nature, only its shape (Physical Change). In the second part, the varnish is a new liquid substance created by processing resin and alcohol together (Chemical Change/Industrial Blend).

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: During the peak of the winter season, the
mechanical gears of the clock tower got
freeze due to the lack of proper lubrication.
No Error
options_hi: During the peak of the winter season, the
mechanical gears of the clock tower got
freeze due to the lack of proper lubrication.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C).

Replace “freeze” with “frozen”.

📌 Rule/Concept: The Passive "Get" and Past Participles –

When we use the verb "get" (or become/be) to describe a change in state or a passive action, it must be followed by the Past Participle (V3) form of the verb, not the base form (V1). The past participle acts as an adjective describing the subject's condition.

V1 (Base): Freeze V2 (Past): Froze V3 (Past Participle): Frozen

💢 Application to the Given Question- In this sentence, "got" indicates a transition into a new state. The gears did not perform the action of freezing; they became in a state of being frozen. Therefore, the base form "freeze" is grammatically incorrect. To describe the state of the gears, we must use the V3 form: frozen.

Incorrect: The water got freeze.

Correct: The water got frozen. (or "The water froze.")

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

The "Done" Rule: Whenever you see Get/Got, Become/Became, or Is/Are/Was/Were, ask yourself if the subject is doing the action or experiencing a state. If it's a state, use V3.

Common "Got" Collocations: Got tired, got bored, got stuck, got broken, got frozen.

Verb vs. Adjective: Remember that while "froze" is a verb (The water froze), "frozen" is the form used after helping verbs to describe the result.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Despite the mounting pressure from the board of directors,
the chief legal officer claims to resolve all the pending litigation issues
during the high-stakes arbitration session held in Singapore last month.
options_hi: Despite the mounting pressure from the board of directors,
the chief legal officer claims to resolve all the pending litigation issues
during the high-stakes arbitration session held in Singapore last month.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “to resolve” with “to have resolved”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Perfect Infinitive (to + have + V3)

In advanced grammar, we must distinguish between the timing of the main verb and the accompanying action (the infinitive).

  • Simple Infinitive (to + V1): Used when the action happens at the same time as or after the main verb.

  • Perfect Infinitive (to + have + V3): Used when the action described by the infinitive was completed before the time of the main verb.



💢 Application to the Given Question

The sentence is long and filled with "distractor" phrases (like mounting pressure and high-stakes arbitration), but the core grammatical structure is: "The officer claims (Present) + to resolve (Past Action)."

  1. Main Verb: "claims" — This is in the present tense. The officer is making the statement now.

  2. Infinitive Action: "resolve" — The sentence explicitly states this happened "last month".

Because the act of resolving the litigation is a finished event from the past, the simple infinitive "to resolve" is incorrect. To bridge the time gap between the present claim and the past event, you must use the perfect infinitive: "to have resolved".

Corrected Sentence

"Despite the mounting pressure from the board of directors, the chief legal officer claims to have resolved all the pending litigation issues during the high-stakes arbitration session held in Singapore last month."

The strict policy does not __________ any deviation from the prescribed procedure.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The strict policy does not __________ any deviation from the prescribed procedure.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (2).

English Explanation: “Allow of” is a formal expression meaning to permit or make something possible, and it is most commonly used in negative constructions such as “does not allow of.” In the sentence, “The strict policy does not ______ any deviation,” the meaning clearly suggests that no deviation is permitted. Therefore, “does not allow of” correctly conveys that there is no scope for exceptions. “Allow for” means to take something into consideration. “Allow in” means to permit someone to enter. “Allow through” means to permit someone or something to pass. Since the context is about permitting or not permitting exceptions, “allow of” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Allow for (ध्यान में रखना / गुंजाइश रखना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी बात को ध्यान में रखना या संभावना को शामिल करना।
Example: We must allow for traffic delays while planning the trip. (यात्रा की योजना बनाते समय हमें ट्रैफिक की देरी को ध्यान में रखना चाहिए।)

2. Allow of (अनुमति देना / संभव बनाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ की अनुमति देना, विशेषकर औपचारिक संदर्भ में।
Example 1: The rules do not allow of any relaxation in the age limit for this examination. (नियम इस परीक्षा में आयु सीमा में किसी भी प्रकार की छूट की अनुमति नहीं देते।)
Example 2: The situation does not allow of further discussion. (स्थिति आगे चर्चा की अनुमति नहीं देती।)

3. Allow in (अंदर आने देना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी को अंदर प्रवेश करने की अनुमति देना।
Example: The guard allowed the visitors in after checking their IDs. (गार्ड ने पहचान पत्र जांचने के बाद आगंतुकों को अंदर आने दिया।)

4. Allow through (गुजरने देना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी को या किसी वस्तु को पार होने की अनुमति देना।
Example: The security check allowed only authorized vehicles through. (सुरक्षा जांच ने केवल अधिकृत वाहनों को गुजरने दिया।)

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Due to the unprecedented severity of the prolonged drought
and the lack of irrigation facilities, the struggling local farmers
only could harvest half of their usual seasonal crop this year.
No Error
options_hi: Due to the unprecedented severity of the prolonged drought
and the lack of irrigation facilities, the struggling local farmers
only could harvest half of their usual seasonal crop this year.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “only could harvest” with “could harvest only”.

Rule / Concept: Position of the Adverb "Only"

the adverb "only" is exceptionally picky about its placement. It must be placed immediately before the word, phrase, or clause it is intended to modify. If it is placed elsewhere, it often attaches itself to the verb, changing the logic of the sentence. In competitive exams, when a sentence highlights a specific quantity (like "half" or "two"), "only" should be positioned to qualify that quantity directly.

Even/only/just/too ; use these words just before the word that it qualifies otherwise meaning will change.

Application to the Given Question

"...the struggling local farmers only could harvest half of their usual seasonal crop..."

In this context, the emphasis is on the scant quantity of the harvest (half). By placing "only" before the auxiliary verb "could," the sentence suggests that the only thing the farmers were capable of doing was harvesting (as if they couldn't even walk or speak). To correctly emphasize that the amount was limited, "only" must be placed immediately before "half."

Corrected Sentence

Due to the unprecedented severity of the prolonged drought and the lack of irrigation facilities, the struggling local farmers could harvest only half of their usual seasonal crop this year.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: She sleeps only five hours a night. (Modifies the number) ✅

Example 2: He only works on weekends. (Modifies the time/action) ✅

Example 3: They invited only the relatives. (Modifies the group) ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: She only sleeps five hours a night. ❌

Wrong example 2: He only has one friend in the city. (Correct: He has only one friend...) ❌

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The hen had lain several eggs
in the corner of the barn before
the farmer arrived this morning.
No Error
options_hi: The hen had lain several eggs
in the corner of the barn before
the farmer arrived this morning.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A).

Replace “lain” with “laid”.

📌 Rule/Concept: Transitive vs. Intransitive Verbs (Lie vs. Lay) -

The confusion arises because the past tense of "Lie" is "Lay." However, they are two distinct verbs:

Lie (Intransitive): To recline or be in a flat position. It does not take an object.

Forms: Lie (V1), Lay (V2), Lain (V3), Lying (V-ing).

Lay (Transitive): To put or place something down. It must have an object.

Forms: Lay (V1), Laid (V2), Laid (V3), Laying (V-ing).

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "several eggs" is the direct object receiving the action of being placed or produced. Therefore, we must use the transitive verb Lay. Since the sentence uses the past perfect tense ("had" + V3), we need the V3 form of "Lay," which is Laid. "Lain" is the V3 of the intransitive verb "Lie" (to recline), which is incorrect here.

More Examples for Clarity -

1- He laid his coat on the bed. (Object: coat)

2- I have lain on this sofa for three hours. (No object; reclining)

3- Please lay the book on the shelf. (Object: book).

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Object Check: If there is a noun/pronoun after the verb (eggs, stress, foundation, book), use Lay/Laid/Laid.

The V3 Trap: Remember that Lain is for resting/reclining, and Laid is for putting/placing.

Action Type: "Lay" requires an actor putting something somewhere. "Lie" describes the state of the subject itself.

questions.solution_en:

📌 Rule / Concept: Stative Verbs in Perfect Tenses -

Stative Verbs (Know, Believe, Own, etc.): As established, these cannot take the -ing form.

💢 Application to the Given Question - "I have been knowing my best friend since we were in primary school."

The sentence uses "since," which correctly indicates a duration. However, the verb Know is a stative verb of mental state. Even though "knowing" is a continuous state from childhood to now, the grammar forbids the form "knowing." Therefore, we must use the Present Perfect form: have known.

options_en: Despite his humble beginnings and lack of
formal education, many villagers consider
him a Dhanwantari of their local community.
options_hi: Despite his humble beginnings and lack of
formal education, many villagers consider
him a Dhanwantari of their local community.
questions.solution_en:
Replace “a” with “the”.

Rule/Concept: Proper Nouns used as Metaphors (Comparison):

Generally, Proper Nouns (names of persons, places, etc.) do not take an article. However, when a Proper Noun is used to represent a specific quality or to compare one person's traits to a famous personality, it acts as a Common Noun. In such cases, if we are comparing 'A' to 'B' to show 'A' is the best or a specific example of that quality in a particular group, we use the definite article 'The'.

Application to the Given Question - Here, the person is being compared to "Dhanwantari" (the deity of medicine) to signify his healing skills within a specific group (the local community). When a person is hailed as the equivalent of a famous figure within a specific domain or location, 'The' is used to denote that specific status.

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The stranded passengers, having no
other alternative in the desert, did
nothing but waiting for the rescue team.
options_hi: The stranded passengers, having no
other alternative in the desert, did
nothing but waiting for the rescue team.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “waiting” with “wait”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Bare Infinitives after "But/Except" (The "Do" Rule)

Do (forms) + nothing but + bare infinitive

When the words "but" or "except" are used to mean "apart from" or "excluding," and they are preceded by any form of the verb do (do, does, did), the verb that follows must be a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to").

This is a specific idiomatic structure: Subject + [do/does/did] + nothing + but/except + V1. Even though the action happened in the past (indicated by "did"), the following verb must remain in the base form, not the continuous (-ing) or past participle form.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...did nothing but waiting for the rescue team."

In this sentence, we have the trigger "did nothing but." The verb following "but" is "waiting," which is a Gerund/Present Participle. According to the rule, since it follows the "do + nothing + but" construction, it must be changed to the base form "wait".

Corrected Sentence

The stranded passengers, having no other alternative in the desert, did nothing but wait for the rescue team.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ He did nothing except laugh at my proposal.

Example 2 ✅ She does nothing but complain about the weather all day.

Example 3 ✅ I did nothing but sit there and watch the sunset.
